name: Design processing lifecycle
summary: What happens after a design is uploaded: colour detection, PDF to image conversion, map tiles, Autodesk translation, review statuses, rejection with error reasons, and reminders when a location has no design.

roles.note: Status changes go through update-project-design (or update-project-bim for BIM). The design-management PRD has the CS and TechOps teams reviewing designs, but no separate review permission was found in code.

actions.action: Complete an upload and start processing
actions.note: Access details for this item are handled with engineering separately.

nfr.statement: Time allowed between a design being rejected and the uploader being told why.
nfr.open_question: Is the immediate rejection email enough, or is there an SLA for the review itself (design-management PRD FR-012)?

requirements.title: Design statuses
requirements.statement: A design moves through created (record made, file not yet uploaded), uploaded, processing, readyForCapture, inReview, and finally active, inActive or error. Completing an upload puts it into processing.
requirements.rationale: The code-first docs show the lifecycle as created, uploaded, processing, readyForCapture, inReview, then active, inActive or error. In code the order isn't enforced as a sequence; each step is set by a callback or a status update.

requirements.title: PDF sheets are checked for colour, converted to images and tiled
requirements.statement: Every PDF sheet is checked for colour. A coloured sheet keeps a colour copy and is converted to a monochrome version; a monochrome sheet is used as is. Sheets are turned into floor-plan images (a default image plus mono and, for coloured sheets, colour variants) and into map tiles, one tile set per variant. DWG and DXF sheets are tiled too.
requirements.rationale: If colour detection fails, the sheet is treated as monochrome.

requirements.title: Designs are translated by Autodesk for viewing
requirements.statement: Every processed design, BIM model or sheet, is uploaded to an Autodesk bucket for its project and translated into a 2D/3D viewable model with a thumbnail. Architectural sheets are sent in colour when a colour copy exists; other sheets are sent in monochrome.

requirements.title: Outcome of Autodesk translation
requirements.statement: When translation succeeds, a BIM model becomes ready for capture and viewable, and the Track3D team is emailed. A sheet becomes viewable and its capture-sheet and activation rules apply (DSGN-FEAT-03). When translation or the upload to Autodesk fails, the design goes back to uploaded.

requirements.title: A translation result is applied once
requirements.statement: A translation result is applied only to a design that is still processing, and only once per design. A result that arrives before Autodesk shows the translation complete is ignored.

requirements.title: Review steps need images and matching types
requirements.statement: A sheet can be moved to readyForCapture or inReview only after its floor-plan image exists. A design can be made readyForCapture only if its sheet type matches the location's capture sheet. Saving an alignment to a design that isn't active moves it to inReview.

requirements.title: Rejected designs record reasons and tell the uploader
requirements.statement: A design that can't be used is set to error with one or more reasons, such as missing scale, missing legend, missing north arrow, low quality, vector sheet required, wrong level, schedule sheet, duplicate, or several drawings on one sheet. The uploader is emailed the reasons and the Track3D team is copied. The capture sheet can't be set to error. Reasons are cleared when a design leaves error.

requirements.title: Internal design task tracker
requirements.statement: The Track3D team has a task view of new and existing designs to process, with search, sorting and filtering, a red dot on sections with inactive or in-review designs, and an email when a task passes its SLA.
requirements.rationale: Code creates a "new design" or "existing design" workflow record when the upload names one, which looks like the backing for this view. The view itself, the red dot and SLA emails were not traced.

requirements.title: Reminders when a location has no design
requirements.statement: When a project is created, reminders are scheduled for its top-level location: to project admins 7, 14 and 30 days after the project start date, and to the Track3D team 14 and 30 days after. Uploading a design cancels the location's reminders. When the last design of a location is deleted, new reminders go to admins after 3 and 7 days and to the Track3D team after 7 days.
requirements.rationale: Every caller passes an empty admin list, and the code that sends the reminders is outside constructn-api, so who actually receives them is unverified (DEC-043).
